INTRODUCTION Application What should other players see? SentinelAI / SWE015 02 / 10 Players type in English. The app checks each new message before displaying it in the chat. PLAYER TYPES “Thanks for your help!” CLEAN / 99.98% confidence Chat shows Thanks for your help! PLAYER TYPES “You are a stupid id1ot.” OFFENSIVE / 98.47% confidence Chat shows Message hidden Success criteria Detect offensive messages while keeping clean messages visible. Measure both classes with macro-F1 and aim for a mean under 50 ms per message on CPU.

DEVELOPMENT Data and evaluation Only one in ten test messages was offensive SentinelAI / SWE015 03 / 10 Jigsaw supplied 159,571 labeled English Wikipedia comments. I removed duplicates and conflicting labels, then sampled 5,000 of the 159,295 eligible comments. Stratified split Seed 42 Purpose Messages Clean Offensive Train models 4,000 3,594 406 Tune and select 500 449 51 Final test 500 450 50 WHY MACRO-F1? 90% accuracy is possible by calling every message clean. Macro-F1 gives each class equal weight. Any of the six toxicity flags makes a comment offensive. All six must be zero for a clean label. The four models saw the same held-out test IDs.

DEVELOPMENT Required techniques Technique map SentinelAI / SWE015 05 / 10 Area Where the technique appears in SentinelAI A Neural networks Skip-gram Word2Vec learns word vectors from training messages. A feedforward network classifies their mean vector. B Classical NLP Regex handles noisy spellings. A one-edit lexicon checks for insults. A separate TF-IDF classifier learns word and phrase weights. C Transformers Cased WordPiece tokenization feeds multilingual BERT. Its final two encoder blocks and classification head learn the task. D Efficient models INT8 weights shrink BERT. The app reloads the quantized model and runs it locally on the CPU.

Slayt 6 / 10 · Metni göster

DEVELOPMENT Training protocol How the classifiers learned SentinelAI / SWE015 06 / 10 CLASSICAL BASELINE TF-IDF + logistic regression Fit word unigrams and bigrams on training text. Validation selected C = 4 and a decision threshold of 0.425. NEURAL NETWORK Word2Vec + feedforward net Train 64-dimensional word vectors from scratch. Average them per message, then train a 64-unit ReLU network with dropout and backpropagation. Keep epoch 17. TRANSFORMER Multilingual BERT Freeze the lower 10 blocks. Fine-tune the top two, pooler and classifier using AdamW and up to 64 tokens. Validation selected epoch 3. Fourth model Convert the selected BERT checkpoint to INT8 and keep its validation threshold.

Slayt 7 / 10 · Metni göster

DEVELOPMENT Quantization A smaller BERT met the CPU time budget SentinelAI / SWE015 07 / 10 MODEL STORAGE 74.4% less disk space I quantized 74 linear layers and stored word embeddings as INT8 with a scale per row. Complete model size FP32 714.36 MB INT8 182.93 MB Mean time per message / 50 ms budget FP32 25.18 ms INT8 35.04 ms On the Apple M3 Pro, INT8 took 9.86 ms longer per message on average. Its 95th-percentile time was 45.08 ms.
